Background (from the session that started this one):
Seven people in kept production chats asked the AI to add geometry; three wanted text (raised "MICKEY", a SNAPON logo on a lip, text embossed on a figure). A new tool, `object_add_shape`, now adds boxes and cylinders as parts or holes, but cannot add text. Reading OrcaSlicer's text code (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/EmbossJob.cpp`, `src/slic3r/GUI/Gizmos/GLGizmoEmboss.cpp`) showed it can't be driven by a tool: it places text only by camera ray or mouse point, builds text data from its own window's style manager (file-local `create_emboss_data_base`), runs as a background job, always opens the text window at the end, and silently substitutes a stand-in mesh when the font fails. Kenneth was offered three options (new entry points in OrcaSlicer's files, building text in JusPrin's own code from libslic3r's public functions, or leaving text out) and asked for this prototype of the second. The full finding is in `object-add-shape-text-finding.md` in the shared notes folder. AGENTS.md's fork rules apply: copying OrcaSlicer behaviour needs a stated justification, so the note must say what is copied and why.

Task:
Prototype adding raised or cut text to an object in JusPrin's own code, so the AI could one day add text such as "MICKEY" on top of a model. Do not change any OrcaSlicer-owned file, and do not build a tool or touch the tool registry yet: this is a prototype to measure whether the approach works.

What to try:
1. Build a text mesh synchronously from a string, using only libslic3r's public functions in `src/libslic3r/Emboss.hpp` (`Emboss::create_font_file`, `text2vshapes`, `polygons2model`, or whatever that header offers for the same job) and a font the app already ships in `resources/fonts/`.
2. Place it on one face of an object, in world millimetres (a centre point, the face's normal, a letter height and a depth), and add it as a part (raised) or a negative part (cut in), the same way `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::add_shapes` adds boxes in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaRegions.cpp` on branch `claude/object-add-shape`. That code is uncommitted; read it at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/object-add-shape`, and do not edit that worktree.
3. Measure, on a spread of cases (short and long strings, letters outside Latin such as Chinese, a font that fails to load, text on a top face and on a side face, on a turned and scaled object): time to build, triangle count, whether the mesh is closed, and whether a slice of the result prints the letters (render a picture of the sliced layer or the model).
4. Check whether OrcaSlicer's own text tool can open and edit the result when the volume also carries `text_configuration` and `emboss_shape` as `GLGizmoEmboss` writes them, and what it takes to fill those in.

Done means: a short findings note in the shared notes folder `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_7a8aabaf-598d-4bd0-83a2-6844cad48410/` with the measurements, pictures, what failed, how much code a real tool would need, and how much of OrcaSlicer's text job it would copy. # Can the AI add text through OrcaSlicer's own text job?

Checked 2026-11-21 on branch claude/object-add-shape (base 066c83b62a), by reading
`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/EmbossJob.hpp/.cpp` and `src/slic3r/GUI/Gizmos/GLGizmoEmboss.cpp`.
Nothing here was run; it is what the code says.

## What OrcaSlicer's text path needs

1. **Placement is a point on the screen.** The two public entries are
   `Emboss::start_create_volume(params, data, mouse_pos)` and
   `start_create_volume_without_position(params, data)`. Both find the spot by
   casting a ray from the camera (mouse position, or the canvas centre and the
   selected object). Neither takes a position or a face in the world. The one
   function that takes a transform, `start_create_volume_job(worker, object,
   volume_tr, data, type, gizmo)`, is file-local (anonymous namespace in
   EmbossJob.cpp).
2. **The text itself comes from the text window's state.** `create_emboss_data_base`
   and `TextDataBase` (font file, style, the glyph-to-shape step) are file-local to
   GLGizmoEmboss.cpp and read the window's `StyleManager`, which is built from
   ImGui glyph ranges and a wxFont. `GLGizmoEmboss::re_emboss` shows a style
   manager can be made outside the window, but only for a volume that already
   holds text.
3. **It is a background job.** The mesh is built on the UI job worker; the tool
   would have to return before the text exists, or wait on the worker.
4. **Its last step always opens the text window and changes the selection.**
   `create_volume` (file-local) asserts the gizmo is Emboss or Svg, selects the
   new volume in the object list and calls `open_gizmo`. A call from the AI
   would leave OrcaSlicer's text window open each time.
5. **A failed font silently becomes a stand-in mesh.** When the text makes no
   shape, `create_mesh` substitutes `resources/data/embossed_text.obj` (or a
   36 x 4 x 2.5 mm cube) and only shows a notification. A tool would have to
   detect that itself, or it would report a success that is not text.

## What adding text would take

- **Through OrcaSlicer (the task's preferred route):** new public entry points in
  two OrcaSlicer-owned files: one in EmbossJob to queue a volume at a given
  transform without opening a window (changes `create_volume`'s existing gizmo
  step, so not purely additive), one in GLGizmoEmboss to build text data from a
  string and a default style without the window; plus a background result in
  the coordinator. That is more than a small additive seam.
- **In JusPrin code only:** build the mesh synchronously from libslic3r's public
  `Emboss::create_font_file`, `text2vshapes` and `polygons2model` with a bundled
  font (`resources/fonts/` has HarmonyOS Sans, NanumGothic, Sarabun), and add it
  on the same volume path as boxes and cylinders. No OrcaSlicer file changes, but
  it copies part of the job's mesh step, which the tool guide forbids without a
  stated reason, and the text is a plain mesh: OrcaSlicer's text tool cannot edit
  it unless JusPrin also writes `text_configuration` and `emboss_shape`.
- **Leave text out** (what was built): the tool says "It cannot add text or
  lettering", and the prompt case `shape-text-not-yet` checks the model says so.

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].
